aws_plugin_configuration.title: AWS Plugin Configuration
aws_plugin_configuration.description: Base configuration for all plugins the AWS module is providing. Note that some parameters will be stored in MongoDB without encryption. Users with required permissions will be able to read them in the configuration dialog on this page.
aws_plugin_configuration.lookups_enabled_label: Run AWS instance detail lookups for IP addresses?
aws_plugin_configuration.lookups_enabled_help: When enabled, a message processor will try to identify IP addresses of your AWS entities (like EC2, ELB, RDS, ...) and add additional information abut the service or instance behind it. It can take up to a minute for a change of this to take effect.
aws_plugin_configuration.access_key_help: Note that this will only be used in encrypted connections but stored in plaintext. Please consult the documentation for suggested rights to assign to the underlying IAM user.
aws_plugin_configuration.secret_key_help: Note that this will only be used in encrypted connections and will be stored encrypted (using the system secret). Please consult the documentation for suggested rights to assign to the underlying IAM user.
aws_plugin_configuration.lookup_regions_help: The AWS instance lookup message processor keeps a table of instances for fast address translation. Define the AWS regions you want to include in the tables. This should be all regions you run AWS services in. Remember that your IAM user needs permission for these regions or you will see warnings in your {{productName}} server logs.
aws_plugin_configuration.proxy_enabled_help: When enabled, we'll access the AWS APIs through the HTTP proxy configured (http_proxy_uri) in your {{productName}} configuration file.Important: You have to restart all AWS inputs for this configuration to take effect.
aws_plugin_configuration.save_error_message: AWS plugin configuration failed with status: {{error}}
aws_plugin_configuration.save_error_title: Could not save AWS plugin configuration.

gcs_setup_info.intro: To setup a Google Cloud Storage backend, the steps are as follows:
gcs_setup_info.step_bucket: Create a Google Cloud Storage Bucket with a unique name - see Google‘s documentation on <bucketsLink>Buckets</bucketsLink>. The default Standard Storage Class is recommended.
gcs_setup_info.step_service_account: Create a Google Cloud Service Account, with permissions to read/write/delete from that Bucket - see Google‘s documentation on <serviceAccountsLink>Service Accounts</serviceAccountsLink>.
gcs_setup_info.step_credentials: Set up Application Default credentials on all Graylog nodes. The method differs depending on how your cluster is hosted - see Google‘s documentation on <adcLink>Setting up Application Default credentials</adcLink>.
gcs_setup_info.step_setup_backend: On this page, you are now ready to set up a Google Cloud Storage Backend. You will need to provide the unique name of the Google Cloud storage created during the first step.

throttling_checkbox.help: If enabled, no new messages will be read from this input until the {{productName}} server catches up with its message load. This is typically useful for inputs reading from files or message queue systems like AMQP or Kafka. If you regularly poll an external system, e.g. via HTTP, you normally want to leave this disabled.

otx_adapter_documentation.intro: The AlienVault OTX data adapter uses the <otxLink>OTX API</otxLink> to lookup indicators for the given key.
otx_adapter_documentation.indicator_description: The OTX API offers several different indicators of compromise (IOCs). You have to select which indicator should be used for this data adapter.
otx_adapter_documentation.ip_auto_detect: The IP Auto-Detect indicator is not an official one. We added that to make it possible to auto-detect the IP address type to allow using the same data adapter for IP v4 and v6 addresses.
otx_adapter_documentation.api_key_description: The OTX API key is used to authenticate API requests. Requests also work if you don't enter an API key, but you will most probably get a smaller request limit. If you use this data adapter for production traffic, please register for an OTX account and get an API key.
otx_adapter_documentation.api_url_description: HTTP URL of the OTX API server. The default setting of https://otx.alienvault.com should not be changed except if you want to run some tests with a custom server.
otx_adapter_documentation.user_agent_description: This will set the User-Agent HTTP header for OTX API requests. You can modify this to include your contact details so the OTX API operators can contact you if there are problems with your API requests.
otx_adapter_documentation.connection_timeout_description: The HTTP connection timeout in milliseconds for the OTX API request. If you set this to a high value and the OTX API connection is slow, processing performance can be affected.
otx_adapter_documentation.write_timeout_description: The HTTP write timeout in milliseconds for the OTX API request. If you set this to a high value and the OTX API connection is slow, processing performance can be affected.
otx_adapter_documentation.read_timeout_description: The HTTP read timeout in milliseconds for the OTX API request. If you set this to a high value and the OTX API connection is slow, processing performance can be affected.

otx_adapter_field_set.indicator_help: The OTX indicator type that should be used for lookups.
otx_adapter_field_set.api_url_help: URL of the OTX API server.
otx_adapter_field_set.user_agent_help: The User-Agent header that should be used for the HTTP request.

whois_adapter_documentation.intro: The whois IP lookup data adapter can request network ownership information for an IP address.
whois_adapter_documentation.connect_timeout_description: The connection timeout for the socket to the whois server in milliseconds. If you set this to a high value, it can affect your processing performance.
whois_adapter_documentation.read_timeout_description: The connection read timeout for the socket to the whois server in milliseconds. If you set this to a high value, it can affect your processing performance.

whois_adapter_field_set.read_timeout_help: WHOIS connection read timeout in milliseconds.
